label: Science fiction
description: A speculative idea explored through people: space, near-future tech or strange science, consistent rules and human stakes.
voice: Close third or first person, past tense; the future is shown through lived-in detail, not explained.
The speculative idea has consistent rules and real consequences.
Technology changes how people behave, talk and work.
No info dumps: explain only what the character would think about now.
Human stakes stay at the centre.
Chapters end on a discovery, a failure or a choice.

structure.guide: A normal day in an abnormal world, broken by a concrete anomaly.
The anomaly becomes the protagonist's problem.
Investigate the idea; the rules become clear.
structure.then: Each chapter pushes the idea further and costs something.

structure.guide: The choice that uses the rules of the idea.

outline_guidance: Each chapter tests the central idea with a concrete event and a human cost.
outline_example: Signal Delay | Aboard the relay ship Kestrel, engineer Priya Nand hears her own voice on a message sent eleven years from now | The crew realises the relay can receive from the future | The message ends with a mayday
worldbuilding: The central idea and its rules
naming: Names that reflect a plausible future mix of cultures.
sample:
The message came in at 03:12 ship time, flagged priority, sender unknown.

Priya played it twice before she let herself believe it.

It was her voice. Older, hoarse, with a crackle she recognised from the Kestrel's aft antenna.

"If you're hearing this," the voice said, "don't reboot the relay."

She looked at the maintenance schedule on her wrist. Relay reboot: 03:30.
